## 10. Current supported surfaces and their boundaries

Snapshot: 2026-10-24. Recheck the linked source when execution occurs if an installation step depends on it. Actual plan, workspace policy, rollout, selected host, and application version can change availability.

| Surface | Documented instruction route | Important boundary | Installation target |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ordinary ChatGPT text on Windows/web/Android | Account Custom Instructions and relevant memory; personality style can influence presentation [O01], [O02], [O03]. | CI is not a guaranteed complete memory system. Project/GPT scopes differ. | One compatible account core; retain unrelated preferences; verify Windows and Android fresh chats. |
| Private ChatGPT Project | Project instructions and accessible project sources [O04]. | Project instructions override global CI. Memory mode is a separate control. | Put the explicit character core in instructions; attach full reference only if useful. |
| GPT-Live in a Project | Project instructions, sources, recent project context are documented [O08]. | Selected voice/prosody still requires audio tests; not every detail is necessarily used. | Strongest documented native route for the same explicit character guidance in text and Live voice. |
| Ordinary Live voice | Available conversation context, supported memory/tools, and tone/pace/style requests [O07]. | Preset personalities do not apply to Live. Do not infer permanent acoustic settings from a textual request. | Preserve selected voice; use compatible account guidance and a brief call direction when needed; test. |
| Advanced/Standard voice | Distinct modes with their own documented behavior [O07]. | Standard is transcription-based; Live has no video/screen-share in the reviewed help. Do not transfer every mode's features. | Configure/test only modes actually used, explicitly label each. |
| Cloud ChatGPT Work | Supported account/project personalization, cloud task context and controls [O09], [O14]. | Connected-PC AGENTS files and local Codex memory are not established cloud-orchestrator configuration. Voice and task models can differ. | Native compatible core through actual supported cloud consumers; inspect and test the cloud task. |
| Local desktop Codex / local task | Actual host instruction/configuration chain and task context [O11], [O12], [O13]. | Local host scope is distinct from cloud Work and ordinary Chat. | Requested executor model/effort where available and a concise local adapter. |
| Existing Morning Light dot | Conversation preferences, relevant ChatGPT memory, separate dot notes [O16], [O17], [O18]. | No demonstrated arbitrary all-powerful dot system-prompt editor; calls get selected context. Custom rules govern actions, not writing style. | Brief the existing dot; verify note/use in a separate task and call. |
| Local Codex CLI/IDE | Effective AGENTS instruction chain, applicable config, optional local memories [O11], [O12], [O13], [O14]. | Actual host matters. Local files do not automatically configure ordinary Chat or Android cloud preferences. | Small inline global adapter, preserve project engineering rules; restart fresh session. |
| Subagents | Parent task context, configured instructions and inherited environment as documented [O15]. | Same public voice does not require identical internal role instructions; no shared-consciousness claim. | Compact packet where user-facing prose is produced; root consistency check. |
| Existing custom GPT | Its own instructions/knowledge [O05]. | Does not inherit account CI, saved memory, or earlier conversations; new personal GPT creation is unavailable in current guidance. | Inventory only if actually used. Do not make a new GPT the foundation. |
| Temporary Chat | Personalized or Unpersonalized selection before the first message [O06]. | These modes differ; temporary conversations do not add memory. | Test chosen scope; do not classify intentional unpersonalized behavior as persona failure. |
| External frontend/API | Explicitly configured application prompt, state, voice, and provider. | Separate application, credentials, costs, routing, and memory. | Optional alternative only after a measured unmet requirement. |

### 10.1 Native facts that affect decisions

- Current CI documentation lists 1,500 characters for Free/Go and 5,000 for Plus/Pro/Business/Enterprise/Education. Inspect the actual field limit; do not infer a plan from ambiguous account labels. The help page's lead says changes apply across chats immediately; some older wording is less clear. Fresh-chat testing remains required [O01].
- Current memory is selective, not a verbatim contract store; a visible summary may be incomplete. Preserve unrelated memories and separate correction from deletion [O02].
- Default-memory Projects are not universally isolated. Project-only is a separate boundary; Work is currently unavailable there. Shared projects have special isolation behavior. Do not relax an existing privacy boundary to get persona consistency [O04].
- Live has documented Project support, including project instructions, since the dated August 7 release note. This is positive evidence for a native persistent behavior route, not a guarantee of identical vocal performance [O08].
- A preset such as Candid/Cynical is not a Lucifer implementation. Use the least conflicting observed baseline; Default is a reasonable candidate when changing the preset is within scope. Inspect actual characteristic controls if present; exact slider names were not verified in this research [O03].
- The current old “ChatGPT agent” help page announces its replacement by Work while retaining some obsolete instructions below. Do not build the plan around an assumed /agent mode [O19].
- Current GPT guidance makes a new custom GPT a poor central investment. Existing GPTs require independent configuration; affected Enterprise GPT retirement is scheduled for December 11, 2026, with other availability governed by actual notices. Do not generalize that date to every account [O05].

### 10.2 Local Codex facts

At startup, Codex builds an instruction chain. Under the actual CODEX_HOME (default ~/.codex), the first applicable global override/base file is used; project instructions then accumulate from repository root toward the current directory, with closer applicable instructions later. The documented default combined project-instruction budget is 32 KiB; project_doc_max_bytes controls it. persona.md is not an automatically discovered magic filename [O11].

Use the documented configuration pair where the target client supports it:

~~~toml
model = "gpt-6.1-sol"
model_reasoning_effort = "high"
~~~

This selects the future executor when effective; it does not select ordinary ChatGPT or acoustic voice. Read actual effective configuration rather than assuming the file wins. Use the documented model selector and status/debug commands available in that client. Do not invent a slash-command argument syntax or silently replace the requested model [O12], [O13], [O23].

The current personality compatibility setting accepts none to omit the built-in Personality section; friendly/pragmatic are deprecated. Changing it is optional only if an observed built-in-style conflict justifies it. Do not replace the full system instructions through model_instructions_file to obtain a persona [O12].

Local Codex memories exist, are separate from ChatGPT memory, and default off. They are unnecessary for loading a small stable character core. Avoid modifying generated memory databases or enabling memory merely because it exists [O14].

Skills use progressive loading; a skill on disk is not an always-loaded persona. Local hooks require reviewed trust, and supported hook behavior differs between local-only execution and cloud orchestration. User local/plugin hooks are not a universal cloud Work/dot injection route. Keep hooks out of the minimum solution [O20], [O21].
